class AWMEnvironmentManager(EnvironmentManagerBase):
    """Prompt/history adapter for AgentWorldModel MCP environments."""

    def __init__(self, envs, projection_f, config):
        self.memory = SimpleMemory()
        self.tasks = []
        super().__init__(envs, projection_f, config)

    def reset(self, kwargs):
        tasks, infos = self.envs.reset(kwargs)
        self.tasks = list(tasks)
        self.memory.reset(batch_size=len(tasks))
        initial = self.build_text_obs(init=True)
        observations = {
            "text": initial,
            "text_base": initial.copy(),
            "image": None,
            "anchor": list(tasks),
        }
        return observations, infos

    def step(self, text_actions: List[str]):
        actions, valids = self.projection_f(text_actions)
        text_obs, rewards, dones, infos = self.envs.step(actions)
        self.memory.store({"action": text_actions, "observation": text_obs})
        next_text = self.build_text_obs()
        for idx, info in enumerate(infos):
            # Preserve semantic MCP errors reported by the bridge while also
            # honoring projection-level format validation.
            info["is_action_valid"] = to_numpy(
                bool(valids[idx]) and bool(info.get("is_action_valid", True))
            )
        return {
            "text": next_text,
            "text_base": next_text.copy(),
            "image": None,
            "anchor": text_obs,
        }, to_numpy(rewards), to_numpy(dones), infos

    def build_text_obs(self, init=False):
        prompts = []
        history_length = int(self.config.env.history_length)
        for idx, task in enumerate(self.tasks):
            if init or not self.memory[idx]:
                prompts.append(AWM_INITIAL_TEMPLATE.format(
                    system_prompt=AWM_SYSTEM_PROMPT, task_description=task,
                ))
                continue
            recent = self.memory[idx][-history_length:] if history_length > 0 else self.memory[idx]
            history = []
            for turn, item in enumerate(recent, 1):
                history.append(f"Assistant {turn}:\n{item['action']}\nTool {turn}:\n{item['observation']}")
            prompts.append(AWM_STEP_TEMPLATE.format(
                system_prompt=AWM_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
                task_description=task,
                history="\n\n".join(history),
            ))
        return prompts

Zhaoyang Wang1, Canwen Xu2, Boyi Liu2, Yite Wang2, Siwei Han1,

# Overview **AgentWorldModel-1K** contains 1,000 fully synthetic, executable, SQL database-backed tool-use environments exposed via a unified MCP (Model Context Protocol) interface, designed for large-scale multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning. Each environment is synthesized through the **Agent World Model (AWM)** pipeline: 1. **Scenario** — A high-level description (e.g., "an online shopping platform") 2. **Tasks** — 10 user tasks per scenario that serve as functional requirements 3. **Database** — SQLite database schema and sample data as the state backend 4. **Interface** — Python interface layer (FastAPI + MCP) as the action/observation space 5. **Verification** — Verification code that inspects database state changes for reward signals For the full synthesis pipeline, please visit [https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model). # Resources Related resources are also available, please check: | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | 📄 Paper | [📄 arxiv.org/abs/2602.10090](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10090) | | 💻 Code | [💻 Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model) | | 📦 AgentWorldModel-1K | [🤗 Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-4B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-8B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-8B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-8B) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-14B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-14B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-14B) | # Agent World Model

Infinity Synthetic Environments for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

Zhaoyang Wang1, Canwen Xu2, Boyi Liu2, Yite Wang2, Siwei Han1,
Zhewei Yao2, Huaxiu Yao1, Yuxiong He2

1UNC-Chapel Hill   2Snowflake AI Research  

Agent World Model (AWM) is a fully synthetic environment generation pipeline that synthesizes 1,000 executable, SQL database-backed tool-use environments exposed via unified MCP interface for large-scale multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning.

--- ## 📣 News - May 1, 2026: AWM got accepted to ICML 2026 🎉, and its infra got merged into [meta-pytorch/OpenEnv](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/OpenEnv) supporting large-scale agentic RL training! Have a live demo try at [huggingface space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ChilleD/agent_world_model_env) 🤗! - Mar 16, 2026: we added the verification demo, please refer to [Verification](#verification) section! - Feb 10, 2026: we open-sourced the synthesis pipeline, 1,000 synthesized environments and RL trained agents at [Huggingface](https://huggingface.co/collections/Snowflake/agent-world-model)! ## 🔮 Resources We released the syntheszied 1,000 executable environments and corresponding tasks, databases, and verification in huggingface. Please checkout huggingface repo at [Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K). You can freely interact with these environments online at [HuggingFace Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ChilleD/agent_world_model_env). | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | 📄 Paper | [📄 arxiv.org/abs/2602.10090](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10090) | | 💻 Code | [💻 Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model) | | ⚓️ RL Infra | [⚓️ meta-pytorch/OpenEnv](https://github.com/meta-pytorch/OpenEnv/tree/main/envs/agent_world_model_env) | | 🛜 Live Demo | [🤗 HuggingFace Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/ChilleD/agent_world_model_env) | | 📦 AgentWorldModel-1K | [🤗 Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-4B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-8B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-8B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-8B) | | 🤖 Arctic-AWM-14B | [🤗 Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-14B](https://huggingface.co/Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-14B) | If you want to directly use our synthesized environments, please download by ```bash hf download Snowflake/AgentWorldModel-1K --repo-type dataset --local-dir ./outputs/ ``` Then you can skip to [Environment Management](#environment-management) and [Agent Demo](#agent-demo) to start using the environments locally. ## 📦 Setup Run `uv sync` to setup the python environment. And set your LLM API credentials: ```bash # OpenAI or any other compatible services export AWM_SYN_LLM_PROVIDER="openai" export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key" # optional, if you are using a custom base url export OPENAI_BASE_URL="http://xxxxxx" # Azure OpenAI export AWM_SYN_LLM_PROVIDER="azure" export AZURE_ENDPOINT_URL="https://your-endpoint.openai.azure.com/" export AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key" # configure the model/LLM for synthesis export AWM_SYN_OVERRIDE_MODEL="your-model-name such as gpt-5" ``` ## 🔥 Synthesis ### AWM CLI All synthesis is exposed through the `awm` command-line tool. Run `awm --help` to see available commands: ``` awm --help Available commands: gen Synthesis pipeline commands ├── scenario Generate scenario names from seed set ├── task Generate user tasks per scenario ├── db Generate database schema and create SQLite databases ├── sample Generate and insert sample data into databases ├── spec Generate API specification for each scenario ├── env Generate MCP environment code ├── verifier Generate verification code for tasks └── all Run the full synthesis pipeline env Environment management commands ├── start Start MCP server for a scenario ├── check Check if an MCP server is running and list its tools ├── check_all Check all generated environments └── reset_db Reset databases to initial state agent Run a tool-use agent to solve a task by interacting with the environment verify Verify agent run outputs using code-augmented LLM-as-a-Judge or purely code-based Judge ``` Use `awm --help` to see options for any command, e.g. `awm gen task --help`. ### Step 1: Scenario Generation We start with a seed set of scenarios and generate 1,000 unique scenario descriptions. Note that only the names are used as seeds; the descriptions are included in the seed file for ease of use. ```bash export EMBEDDING_OPENAI_API_KEY="your-api-key for the embedding model" awm gen scenario \ --input_path outputs/seed_scenario.jsonl \ --output_path outputs/gen_scenario.jsonl \ --target_count 1000 ``` ### Step 2: Task Generation We generate 10 tasks per scenario, which are also serving as the requirements for building the environment. ```bash awm gen task \ --input outputs/gen_scenario.jsonl \ --output outputs/gen_tasks.jsonl ``` ### Step 3: Database Synthesis We define the database schema and complete the initial state to fully support the generated tasks. ```bash # database schema awm gen db \ --input outputs/gen_tasks.jsonl \ --output outputs/gen_db.jsonl # sample data for initial state awm gen sample \ --input_task outputs/gen_tasks.jsonl \ --input_db outputs/gen_db.jsonl \ --output outputs/gen_sample.jsonl ``` ### Step 4: Interface Synthesis We first generate API spec for better generating the Python code of the environment in MCP interface. ```bash # API spec (interface schema) awm gen spec \ --input_task outputs/gen_tasks.jsonl \ --input_db outputs/gen_db.jsonl \ --output outputs/gen_spec.jsonl # Environment code awm gen env \ --input_spec outputs/gen_spec.jsonl \ --input_db outputs/gen_db.jsonl \ --output outputs/gen_envs.jsonl ``` ### Step 5: Verification Synthesis We provide two options for verification: 1. code-augmented LLM-as-a-Judge (`sql`) 2. purely code-based Judge (`code`) ```bash awm gen verifier \ --mode sql \ --input_task outputs/gen_tasks.jsonl \ --output outputs/gen_verifier.jsonl ``` ### Environment Management Run and check each environment. The MCP endpoint will be available at `http://localhost:8001/mcp`. ```bash # Reset databases to initial state awm env reset_db \ --input_db outputs/gen_db.jsonl \ --input_sample outputs/gen_sample.jsonl # Start MCP server for a scenario awm env start \ --scenario "scenario_name" \ --envs_load_path outputs/gen_envs.jsonl \ --port 8001 # Check if MCP server is running awm env check --url http://localhost:8001/mcp # Batch test all generated environments awm env check_all --output outputs/gen_envs.jsonl ``` ### Agent Demo AWM includes a simple agent demo that connects to an MCP environment to solve tasks via multi-turn tool calling. Please start the environment and use [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) to serve the model before running the agent. ```bash # serve the model vllm serve Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 # start the environment, this will create an isolated folder outputs/servers/ to save the environment related files such as initial.db, final.db, and etc. awm env start --scenario e_commerce_33 --envs_load_path outputs/gen_envs.jsonl --port 8001 # run the agent awm agent \ --task "show me the top 10 most expensive products" \ --mcp_url http://localhost:8001/mcp \ --api_url http://localhost:8000/v1 \ --model Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B ``` ### Verification AWM supports two types of verification: 1. `sql`, the recommended code-augmented LLM-as-a-Judge (requires LLM env vars, see Setup section) 2. `code`, purely code-based Judge ```bash # launch an isolated environment and run the agent to finish the task of corresponding scenario awm agent \ --scenario e_commerce_33 \ --task_id 0 \ --api_url http://localhost:8000/v1 \ --model Snowflake/Arctic-AWM-4B # after interaction, the trajectory will be saved to outputs/agents/, we can verify it by awm verify --input outputs/agents/ --mode sql ``` ## Citation If you find this work useful, please kindly cite: ```bibtex @article{wang2026agentworldmodelinfinity, title={Agent World Model: Infinity Synthetic Environments for Agentic Reinforcement Learning}, author={Zhaoyang Wang and Canwen Xu and Boyi Liu and Yite Wang and Siwei Han and Zhewei Yao and Huaxiu Yao and Yuxiong He}, year={2026}, eprint={2602.10090}, archivePrefix={arXiv}, primaryClass={cs.AI}, url={https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.10090}, } ``` # IDEA IDEA is the submitter's project for agentic reinforcement learning with on-policy self-distillation. This source tree contains the IDEA implementation used for the recorded Agent World Model (AWM) OPSD experiment in this contribution. The project name is IDEA. Source paths use `idea_source/`, the Python package is `idea`, and training scripts live in `examples/idea_trainer/`. The historical `algorithm.seed` configuration namespace, analyzer class names, prompt-version values and metric keys are retained for runtime compatibility. Recorded numerical evidence and upstream attribution remain unchanged. ## Recorded task entry point Run the contribution's `workspace/run_local.sh` wrapper from the workspace root. It uses `reproduce.py` and the recorded Hydra configuration under `config/.hydra/`. Training is optional and requires separately provisioned model weights, dependencies, and hardware; static issue diagnosis does not require a training rerun. The release includes only the AWM environment package; unrelated environment implementations, site documentation and presentation images are omitted. The AWM, IDEA and veRL execution path is retained. Data inputs and complete server/trajectory logs are directly readable original files. The optional preparation check verifies SHA-256 and byte sizes only; it never extracts or rewrites files. No compressed release assets or network downloads are needed. ## Components - `agent_system/`: agent environments and multi-turn rollout integration. - `verl/`: veRL-based training implementation. - `idea/`: trajectory analysis and distillation modules. - `examples/idea_trainer/`: training launch scripts, including AWM OPSD. - `../awm_source/`: the separately supplied Agent World Model runtime. ## License and upstream attribution Retain `LICENSE`, `Notice.txt`, file-level copyright notices, and nested third-party licenses.         from PIL import Image

from verl import DataProto
import torch
import numpy as np

class EpisodeRewardManager:
    """The reward manager.
    """

    def __init__(self, tokenizer, num_examine, normalize_by_length=False) -> None:
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.num_examine = num_examine  # the number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console
        self.normalize_by_length = normalize_by_length

    def __call__(self, data: DataProto, return_dict=False):
        """We will expand this function gradually based on the available datasets"""

        # If there is rm score, we directly return rm score. Otherwise, we compute via rm_score_fn
        if "rm_scores" in data.batch.keys():
            if return_dict:
                return {"reward_tensor": data.batch["rm_scores"]}
            else:
                return data.batch["rm_scores"]

        reward_tensor = torch.zeros_like(data.batch['responses'], dtype=torch.float32)

        already_print_data_sources = {}

        for i in range(len(data)):
            data_item = data[i]  # DataProtoItem

            prompt_ids = data_item.batch['prompts']

            prompt_length = prompt_ids.shape[-1]

            valid_prompt_length = data_item.batch['attention_mask'][:prompt_length].sum()
            valid_prompt_ids = prompt_ids[-valid_prompt_length:]

            response_ids = data_item.batch['responses']
            valid_response_length = data_item.batch['attention_mask'][prompt_length:].sum()
            valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]

            # decode
            prompt_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_prompt_ids, skip_special_tokens=False)
            response_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_response_ids, skip_special_tokens=False)

            # ground_truth = data_item.non_tensor_batch['reward_model']['ground_truth']

            data_source = data_item.non_tensor_batch['data_source']

            extra_info = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get('extra_info', None)
            multi_modal_inputs = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get('multi_modal_inputs', None)
            if multi_modal_inputs is not None:
                pixel_values = multi_modal_inputs['pixel_values']
                image_grid_thw = multi_modal_inputs['image_grid_thw']


            episode_rewards = data_item.non_tensor_batch['episode_rewards']
            episode_lengths = data_item.non_tensor_batch['episode_lengths']

            if self.normalize_by_length:
                score = episode_rewards / episode_lengths
            else:
                score = episode_rewards
            reward_tensor[i, valid_response_length - 1] = torch.tensor(score, dtype=torch.float32, device=prompt_ids.device)

            if data_source not in already_print_data_sources:
                already_print_data_sources[data_source] = 0

            if already_print_data_sources[data_source] < self.num_examine and np.random.random() < 0.1:
                already_print_data_sources[data_source] += 1
                print(f"[{data_source}][prompt]", prompt_str)
                print(f"[{data_source}][response]", response_str)
                print(f"[{data_source}][score]", score)

        if return_dict:
            return {
                "reward_tensor": reward_tensor,
                "reward_extra_info": {},
            }
        else:
            return reward_tensor

from typing import List, Tuple, Dict, Union, Any
import torch
import numpy as np
import os
from agent_system.environments.prompts import *
from collections import defaultdict

def to_numpy(data):
    if isinstance(data, torch.Tensor):
        data = data.detach().cpu().numpy()
    elif isinstance(data, np.ndarray):
        pass
    elif isinstance(data, (int, float, bool, Tuple, List)):
        data = np.array(data)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported type: {type(data)})")
    return data

class EnvironmentManagerBase:
    def __init__(self, envs, projection_f, config):
        """
        Initialize the environment manager.
        
        Parameters:
        - envs: The environment instance, usually a vectorized environment containing multiple sub-environments.
        - projection_f: A function that maps text actions to environment actions.
        - config: Configuration object.
        """
        self.envs = envs
        self.projection_f = projection_f
        self.config = config
        self._seed_use_with_memory = False

    def set_seed_use_with_memory(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
        self._seed_use_with_memory = bool(enabled)

    def reset(self, kwargs) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Reset all environments and return the initial observations.
        Parameters:
        - kwargs (Dict): Additional keyword arguments for resetting the environment.

        Returns:
        - next_observations (Dict):
          - 'text' (None or List[str]): The textual observation.
          - 'image' (np.ndarray or torch.Tensor): The image observation as either a NumPy array or a PyTorch tensor.
          - 'anchor' (None or Any): Anchor observation without any histories or additional info. (for GiGPO only).
        """
        obs, infos = self.envs.reset()
        return {'text': None, 'image': obs, 'anchor': None}, infos
    
    def step(self, text_actions: List[str]):
        """
        Execute text actions and return the next state, rewards, done flags, and additional information.
        
        Parameters:
        - text_actions (List[str]): A list of text actions to execute.
        
        Returns:
        - next_observations (Dict):
          - 'text' (None or List[str]): The textual observation.
          - 'image' (np.ndarray or torch.Tensor): The image observation as either a NumPy array or a PyTorch tensor.
          - 'anchor' (None or Any): Anchor observation without any histories or additional info. (for GiGPO only).
        - rewards (np.ndarry or torch.Tensor): The rewards returned by the environment.
        - dones (np.ndarray or torch.Tensor): Done flags indicating which environments have completed.
        - infos (List[Dict]): Additional environment information.
        
        Exceptions:
        - NotImplementedError: If an observation key is not in ('text', 'image').
        """
        actions, valids = self.projection_f(text_actions)
        next_obs, rewards, dones, infos = self.envs.step(actions)

        next_observations = {
            'text': None, # Implement this if needed
            'image': next_obs,
            'anchor': None # For GiGPO/SEED only. anchor observation without histories, injected skills, etc. Implement this if needed
        }
        # add action_valid to infos
        for i, info in enumerate(infos):
            info['is_action_valid'] = to_numpy(valids[i])

        rewards = to_numpy(rewards)
        dones = to_numpy(dones)
        
        return next_observations, rewards, dones, infos

    def build_text_obs(self,) -> List[str]:
        """
        This function builds the text observation for the agent.
        
        Returns:
        - postprocess_text_obs (List[str]): A list of processed text observations.
        """
        pass

    def close(self) -> None:
        """
        Close the environment and release resources.
        """
        self.envs.close()

    def close_sessions(self) -> None:
        close_sessions = getattr(self.envs, "close_sessions", None)
        if close_sessions is not None:
            close_sessions()

    def success_evaluator(self, *args, **kwargs) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Evaluate if the episodes are successful or not. 
        (Default) implementation is to check info['won'] of the last step.
        
        Returns:

    def _process_batch(self, batch_idx, total_batch_list, total_infos, success):
        for i in reversed(range(len(total_batch_list[batch_idx]))):
            batch_item = total_batch_list[batch_idx][i]
            if batch_item['active_masks']:
                info = total_infos[batch_idx][i]
                won_value = float(info['won'])
                success['success_rate'].append(won_value)
                return

Determine the top 3 best-selling among qualifying_ids\n    # Sorting rules:\n    #   - Primary: sales_rank ascending, treating NULL as worse than any number\n    #   - Secondary: product_id ascending for deterministic tie-breaking\n\n    def sort_key(pid):\n        sr = rank_map.get(pid)\n        if sr is None:\n            # Use a large sentinel for NULL ranks\n            return (10**12, pid)\n        # Ensure numeric\n        try:\n            sr_val = float(sr)\n        except Exception:\n            # If somehow non-numeric, treat as worst\n            return (10**12, pid)\n        return (sr_val, pid)\n\n    sorted_ids = sorted(qualifying_ids, key=sort_key)\n\n    if len(sorted_ids) < 3:\n        # Defensive check; should already be covered but keep it safe\n        return {\"result\": \"others\"}\n\n    top_three_ids = sorted_ids[:3]\n\n    # 8. # Overview

**AgentWorldModel-1K** contains 1,000 fully synthetic, executable, SQL database-backed tool-use environments exposed via a unified MCP (Model Context Protocol) interface, designed for large-scale multi-turn agentic reinforcement learning.

Each environment is synthesized through the **Agent World Model (AWM)** pipeline:

1. **Scenario** — A high-level description (e.g., "an online shopping platform")
2. **Tasks** — 10 user tasks per scenario that serve as functional requirements
3. **Database** — SQLite database schema and sample data as the state backend
4. **Interface** — Python interface layer (FastAPI + MCP) as the action/observation space
5. **Verification** — Verification code that inspects database state changes for reward signals

For the full synthesis pipeline, please visit [https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model](https://github.com/Snowflake-Labs/agent-world-model).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prepare a relocated recorded config, check inputs, or launch the issue run."""

import argparse
import importlib.util
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import runpy
import re
import shutil
import tempfile
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from omegaconf import OmegaConf

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "idea_source"))


def runtime_defaults():
    """Optional machine-local paths, never credentials or historical evidence."""
    path = ROOT.parent / "runtime.local.json"
    if not path.is_file():
        return {}
    values = json.loads(path.read_text())
    unknown = set(values) - {"awm_python", "model_path", "model_revision", "dataset_revision"}
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError("Unsupported runtime.local.json keys: " + ", ".join(sorted(unknown)))
    return values


def hub_token():
    if os.environ.get("HF_TOKEN"):
        return os.environ["HF_TOKEN"]
    path = os.environ.get("HF_TOKEN_PATH")
    return Path(path).read_text().strip() if path else None


def immutable_revision(value):
    if not value or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{40}", value):
        raise ValueError("Downloads require a 40-character immutable HF commit SHA")
    return value


def download_data(repo_id, revision):
    from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
    immutable_revision(revision)
    snapshot = Path(snapshot_download(repo_id, repo_type="dataset", revision=revision, token=hub_token(),
                                     allow_patterns=["rl/*", "runtime/*", "manifest.json"]))
    root = ROOT / "data/AgentWorldModel-1K"
    mapping = [(snapshot / "rl/train.parquet", root / "verl/train.parquet"),
               (snapshot / "rl/validation.parquet", root / "verl/test.parquet")]
    names = ["gen_db", "gen_envs", "gen_sample", "gen_tasks", "gen_verifier.pure_code"]
    mapping += [(snapshot / "runtime" / (name + ".jsonl"), root / (name + ".jsonl")) for name in names]
    for source, target in mapping:
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if not target.exists():
            shutil.copy2(source, target)
    manifest = json.loads((ROOT.parent / "environment/data_manifest.json").read_text())
    expected = {item["path"]: item for item in manifest["files"]}
    for _, target in mapping:
        item = expected[target.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()]
        with target.open("rb") as stream:
            digest = hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
        if target.stat().st_size != item["bytes"] or digest != item["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError("Restored data differs from historical inputs: " + target.name)


def prepare(args):
    original = OmegaConf.load(ROOT / "config/.hydra/config.yaml")
    config = OmegaConf.create(OmegaConf.to_container(original, resolve=False))
    data = ROOT / "data/AgentWorldModel-1K"
    output = Path(args.output).absolute()
    python = Path(args.awm_python).absolute()
    model = Path(args.model_path).expanduser()
    if not model.is_dir():
        if model.is_absolute() or args.model_path.startswith("."):
            raise FileNotFoundError(model)
        immutable_revision(args.model_revision)
        from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
        model = Path(snapshot_download(args.model_path, revision=args.model_revision, token=hub_token(),
                                       local_dir=ROOT / "models/IDEA_sft"))
    model = model.absolute()
    config.data.train_files = str(data / "verl/train.parquet")
    config.data.val_files = str(data / "verl/test.parquet")
    config.actor_rollout_ref.model.path = str(model)
    config.env.awm.root = str(ROOT / "awm_source")
    config.env.awm.python = str(python)
    config.env.awm.data_root = str(data)
    config.env.awm.work_root = str(output / "awm_runtime")
    # Code rewards do not use a hosted judge; never carry a recorded credential
    # into a new config or console log.
    config.env.awm.judge_api_key = (
        os.environ.get("AWM_JUDGE_API_KEY", "EMPTY")
        if config.env.awm.reward_mode == "sql" else "EMPTY"
    )
    if config.env.awm.reward_mode == "sql" and config.env.awm.judge_api_key == "EMPTY":
        raise RuntimeError("SQL reward mode requires AWM_JUDGE_API_KEY")
    for field, folder in (("analysis_dump_dir", "idea_analysis"),
                          ("augmented_observation_dump_dir", "idea_augmented_observations"),
                          ("state_group_dump_dir", "idea_state_group")):
        config.algorithm.seed[field] = str(output / folder)
    config.trainer.rollout_data_dir = str(output / "rollouts")
    config.trainer.default_local_dir = str(output / "checkpoints")
    config.trainer.resume_mode = "disable"
    config.trainer.resume_from_path = None
    output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OmegaConf.resolve(config)
    OmegaConf.save(config, output / "config.yaml")
    return config, output


def check(config):
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
    data = Path(config.env.awm.data_root)
    required = ["gen_tasks", "gen_envs", "gen_db", "gen_sample", "gen_verifier.pure_code"]
    records = {}
    for name in required:
        with (data / f"{name}.jsonl").open() as stream:
            records[name] = [json.loads(line) for line in stream if line.strip()]
    scenarios = {name: {row["scenario"] for row in rows} for name, rows in records.items()}
    tasks = {row["scenario"]: row["tasks"] for row in records["gen_tasks"]}
    splits = {}
    keys = {}
    for split in ("train", "test"):
        rows = pq.read_table(data / f"verl/{split}.parquet").to_pylist()
        keys[split] = set()
        for row in rows:
            item = row["env_kwargs"]
            scenario, index = item["scenario"], item["task_idx"]
            assert item["task"] == tasks[scenario][index], (scenario, index)
            assert all(scenario in values for values in scenarios.values()), scenario
            keys[split].add((scenario, index))
        assert len(keys[split]) == len(rows), f"duplicate {split} task"
        splits[split] = rows
    assert not keys["train"] & keys["test"], "train/test overlap"
    assert len(keys["train"] | keys["test"]) == sum(len(t) for t in tasks.values())
    model = Path(config.actor_rollout_ref.model.path)
    for filename in ("config.json", "tokenizer.json", "tokenizer_config.json"):
        if not (model / filename).is_file():
            raise FileNotFoundError(model / filename)
    if not list(model.glob("*.safetensors")) and not list(model.glob("pytorch_model*.bin")):
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Model weights not found in {model}")
    if not Path(config.env.awm.python).is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(config.env.awm.python)
    return splits, {"split_rows": {k: len(v) for k, v in splits.items()},
                    "scenario_counts": {k: len(v) for k, v in scenarios.items()},
                    "task_alignment": "passed", "train_test_overlap": 0,
                    "model_config_and_weights_present": True}


def smoke(config, output, splits):
    # Load the packaged environment directly, without importing unrelated envs.
    path = ROOT / "idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/envs.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("packaged_awm_env", path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    selected = []
    seen = set()
    for rows in (splits["train"], splits["test"], splits["train"][1:]):
        for row in rows:
            item = row["env_kwargs"]
            if item["scenario"] not in seen:
                selected.append(item)
                seen.add(item["scenario"])
                break
    env = module.AWMMCPVectorEnv(len(selected), 1, config.env)
    try:
        tasks, _ = env.reset(selected)
        observations, _, dones, infos = env.step([{"name": "list_tools", "arguments": None}] * len(selected))
        for item, observation, done, info in zip(selected, observations, dones, infos):
            if done or info.get("reward_type") == "environment_error":
                raise RuntimeError(f"Environment startup failed: {item['scenario']}: {info}")
            assert observation, "empty tool listing"
        _, rewards, dones, infos = env.step([{"name": "final", "content": "Smoke test, no task actions performed."}] * len(selected))
        assert all(dones), "final action did not terminate"
        for item, info in zip(selected, infos):
            if info.get("reward_type") in {"environment_error", "judge_error", "server_error"}:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Verifier failed: {item['scenario']}: {info}")
        return [{"scenario": item["scenario"], "task_idx": item["task_idx"],
                 "reset": bool(task), "list_tools": "passed", "final": "passed",
                 "reward": reward, "reward_type": info.get("reward_type")}
                for item, task, reward, info in zip(selected, tasks, rewards, infos)]
    finally:
        env.close()


def main():
    defaults = runtime_defaults()
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--model-path", default=os.environ.get("MODEL_PATH", defaults.get("model_path", "locaszzz/IDEA_sft")))
    parser.add_argument("--model-revision", default=os.environ.get("MODEL_REVISION", defaults.get("model_revision")))
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-revision", default=os.environ.get("DATASET_REVISION", defaults.get("dataset_revision")))
    parser.add_argument("--dataset-repo", default="locaszzz/IDEA_training_data")
    parser.add_argument("--download-data", action="store_true", help="Fetch RL/runtime inputs from the Hub dataset if absent; authenticate only if required")
    parser.add_argument("--awm-python", default=os.environ.get("AWM_PYTHON", defaults.get("awm_python", "/opt/awm/bin/python")))
    parser.add_argument("--output", default=str(ROOT / "reproduction" / datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ")))
    parser.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true", help="Test MCP startup, list_tools, and code verifier; no model inference")
    mode = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    mode.add_argument("--train", action="store_true", help="Launch the recorded 200-step issue configuration; requires 8 free 80GB GPUs")
    mode.add_argument("--config-only", action="store_true", help="Also check Hydra composition without starting Ray or training")
    args, overrides = parser.parse_known_args()
    if overrides and not (args.train or args.config_only):
        parser.error("Hydra overrides require --train or --config-only")
    if args.download_data:
        download_data(args.dataset_repo, args.dataset_revision)
    if not Path(args.awm_python).is_file():
        parser.error("Set AWM_PYTHON or configure runtime.local.json with the separate AWM interpreter")
    config, output = prepare(args)
    splits, report = check(config)
    report["python"] = sys.executable
    report["scope"] = "input checks; NOT a completed training run"
    if args.smoke:
        report["environment_smoke"] = smoke(config, output, splits)
        import verl.workers.fsdp_workers as workers
        tests = runpy.run_path(str(ROOT / "idea_source/tests/test_awm_projection.py"))
        names = [name for name in tests if name.startswith("test_")]
        for name in names:
            tests[name]()
        report["fsdp_workers_import"] = str(Path(workers.__file__).relative_to(ROOT))
        report["projection_tests_passed"] = len(names)
    (output / "checks.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2), flush=True)
    if args.train or args.config_only:
        env = os.environ.copy()
        env["PYTHONPATH"] = str(ROOT / "idea_source")
        env["PATH"] = f"{Path(sys.executable).parent}:{env.get('PATH', '')}"
        env.setdefault("WANDB_MODE", "offline")
        env["WANDB_DIR"] = str(output)
        env.setdefault("TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM", "false")
        env.setdefault("VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND", "FLASH_ATTN")
        env.setdefault("NCCL_IB_DISABLE", "1")
        env.setdefault("NCCL_P2P_DISABLE", "0")
        env.setdefault("TORCH_NCCL_BLOCKING_WAIT", "1")
        ray_root = os.environ.get("RAY_TMPDIR")
        env["RAY_TMPDIR"] = ray_root or str(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / f"i4ray-{os.getpid()}")
        Path(env["RAY_TMPDIR"]).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        for name in ("http_proxy", "https_proxy", "HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY", "all_proxy", "ALL_PROXY"):
            env.pop(name, None)
        command = [sys.executable, "-m", "verl.trainer.main_ppo", "--config-path", str(output), "--config-name", "config"]
        command += ["hydra.run.dir=" + str(output)]
        if args.config_only:
            command += ["--cfg", "job"]
        command += overrides
        log_path = output / ("hydra-check.log" if args.config_only else "train.log")
        with log_path.open("wb") as log:
            result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=ROOT / "idea_source", env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        (output / "exit-status.json").write_text(json.dumps({"exit_code": result.returncode, "config_only": args.config_only}) + "\n")
        print(f"Exit code: {result.returncode}; combined stdout/stderr: {log_path}")
        return result.returncode
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

   238	def batch_test_environments(env_configs: list[dict], max_workers: int = 8) -> list[tuple[bool, str, dict]]:
   239	    if not env_configs:
   240	        return []
   241	    
   242	    logger.info(f"testing {len(env_configs)} environments in parallel (max_workers={max_workers})...")
   243	    
   244	    results: list[tuple[bool, str, dict]] = [None] * len(env_configs)
   245	    passed = 0
   246	    failed = 0
   247	    
   248	    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:
   249	        future_to_idx = {   
   250	            executor.submit(test_run_specific_env, idx, config): idx
   251	            for idx, config in enumerate(env_configs)
   252	        }
   253	        
   254	        pbar = tqdm(total=len(env_configs), desc="Testing envs", unit="env")
   255	        pbar.set_postfix(passed=passed, failed=failed)
   256	        
   257	        for future in as_completed(future_to_idx):
   258	            idx = future_to_idx[future]
   259	            try:
   260	                result = future.result()
   261	                results[idx] = result
   262	                scenario_name = env_configs[idx]['scenario']
   263	                if result[0]:
   264	                    passed += 1
   265	                    logger.debug(f"{scenario_name}: test passed")
   266	                else:
   267	                    failed += 1
   268	                    logger.debug(f"{scenario_name}: test failed due to {result}")
   269	            except Exception as e:
   270	                failed += 1
   271	                logger.error(f"test execution failed for index {idx}: {e}")
   272	                results[idx] = (False, str(e), env_configs[idx])
   273	            
   274	            pbar.set_postfix(passed=passed, failed=failed)
   275	            pbar.update(1)
   276	        
   277	        pbar.close()
   278	    
   279	    logger.info(f"batch test done: {passed} passed, {failed} failed out of {len(env_configs)} total")
   280	    return results

const r = await tools.exec_command({cmd:"python - <<'PY'
import json,glob,collections,os,re,statistics
for f in sorted(glob.glob('logs/rollouts/*.jsonl')):
 rows=[json.loads(x) for x in open(f)]
 print('\n===',f,'rows',len(rows),'steps',sorted(set(r['step'] for r in rows)))
 by=collections.defaultdict(list)
 for r in rows: by[r['traj_uid']].append(r)
 print('traj',len(by))
 scores=[]; actvalid=0; lens=[]; calls=[]; terminals=[]
 for uid,rs in by.items():
  # order step_num
  rs=sorted(rs,key=lambda r:r['step_num'])
  scores.append(max(float(r.get('score',0)) for r in rs))
  lens.append(len(rs)); calls.append(sum(bool(r.get('is_action_valid')) for r in rs))
  terminals.append(rs[-1])
  actvalid+=sum(bool(r.get('is_action_valid')) for r in rs)
 print('score dist',collections.Counter(scores),'mean',statistics.mean(scores) if scores else None,'lens',collections.Counter(lens),'valid frac',actvalid/len(rows))
 # each terminal snippets
 for r in terminals[:10]: print('sid',r['sample_id'],'rid',r['rollout_id'],'len',len(by[r['traj_uid']]),'score',r['score'],'last_valid',r.get('is_action_valid'),'out',repr(r['output'][:160]))
 # action patterns all outputs, parse names
 c=collections.Counter()
 for r in rows:
  m=re.search(r'"name"\s*:\s*"([^"]+)"',r.get('output',''))
  c[m.group(1) if m else 'final/invalid']+=1
 print('actions',c)

from verl import DataProto
import torch
import numpy as np

class EpisodeRewardManager:
    """The reward manager.
    """

    def __init__(self, tokenizer, num_examine, normalize_by_length=False) -> None:
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.num_examine = num_examine  # the number of batches of decoded responses to print to the console
        self.normalize_by_length = normalize_by_length

    def __call__(self, data: DataProto, return_dict=False):
        """We will expand this function gradually based on the available datasets"""

        # If there is rm score, we directly return rm score. Otherwise, we compute via rm_score_fn
        if "rm_scores" in data.batch.keys():
            if return_dict:
                return {"reward_tensor": data.batch["rm_scores"]}
            else:
                return data.batch["rm_scores"]

        reward_tensor = torch.zeros_like(data.batch['responses'], dtype=torch.float32)

        already_print_data_sources = {}

        for i in range(len(data)):
            data_item = data[i]  # DataProtoItem

            prompt_ids = data_item.batch['prompts']

            prompt_length = prompt_ids.shape[-1]

            valid_prompt_length = data_item.batch['attention_mask'][:prompt_length].sum()
            valid_prompt_ids = prompt_ids[-valid_prompt_length:]

            response_ids = data_item.batch['responses']
            valid_response_length = data_item.batch['attention_mask'][prompt_length:].sum()
            valid_response_ids = response_ids[:valid_response_length]

            # decode
            prompt_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_prompt_ids, skip_special_tokens=False)
            response_str = self.tokenizer.decode(valid_response_ids, skip_special_tokens=False)

            # ground_truth = data_item.non_tensor_batch['reward_model']['ground_truth']

            data_source = data_item.non_tensor_batch['data_source']

            extra_info = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get('extra_info', None)
            multi_modal_inputs = data_item.non_tensor_batch.get('multi_modal_inputs', None)
            if multi_modal_inputs is not None:
                pixel_values = multi_modal_inputs['pixel_values']
                image_grid_thw = multi_modal_inputs['image_grid_thw']


            episode_rewards = data_item.non_tensor_batch['episode_rewards']
            episode_lengths = data_item.non_tensor_batch['episode_lengths']

            if self.normalize_by_length:
                score = episode_rewards / episode_lengths
            else:
                score = episode_rewards
            reward_tensor[i, valid_response_length - 1] = torch.tensor(score, dtype=torch.float32, device=prompt_ids.device)

            if data_source not in already_print_data_sources:
                already_print_data_sources[data_source] = 0

            if already_print_data_sources[data_source] < self.num_examine and np.random.random() < 0.1:
                already_print_data_sources[data_source] += 1
                print(f"[{data_source}][prompt]", prompt_str)
                print(f"[{data_source}][response]", response_str)
                print(f"[{data_source}][score]", score)

        if return_dict:
            return {
                "reward_tensor": reward_tensor,
                "reward_extra_info": {},
            }
        else:
            return reward_tensor

import json
import re
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple


_TOOL_CALL_PATTERN = re.compile(r"<tool_call>\s*(.*?)\s*</tool_call>", re.DOTALL)
_THINK_CLOSE = "</think>"


def _payload_after_think(action: str, require_think: bool) -> Optional[str]:
    """Return the text that may contain a tool call / final answer.

    Tool-call extraction only looks after the first ``</think>``.  Content
    inside the reasoning block is ignored.  A missing close tag is a format
    failure when thinking is required.
    """
    close_idx = action.lower().find(_THINK_CLOSE)
    if close_idx == -1:
        if require_think:
            return None
        return action
    return action[close_idx + len(_THINK_CLOSE) :]


def awm_projection(actions: List[str], require_think: bool = False) -> Tuple[List[dict], List[int]]:
    """Parse the single MCP meta-tool call emitted by the AWM agent prompt.

    When thinking is enabled, an incomplete reasoning block is a format
    failure, just like malformed tool-call JSON.  Tool-call / final-answer
    parsing uses only the suffix after ``</think>``.
    """
    projected = []
    valid = []
    for action in actions:
        payload = _payload_after_think(action, require_think=require_think)
        if payload is None:
            projected.append({"name": "invalid", "content": action})
            valid.append(0)
            continue
        matches = _TOOL_CALL_PATTERN.findall(payload)
        if not matches:
            content = payload.strip()
            projected.append({"name": "final", "content": content})
            valid.append(1 if content else 0)
            continue
        try:
            call = json.loads(matches[0])
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
            projected.append({"name": "invalid", "content": action})
            valid.append(0)
            continue
        name = call.get("name", "") if isinstance(call, dict) else ""
        arguments = call.get("arguments") if isinstance(call, dict) else None
        if name not in {"list_tools", "call_tool"} or len(matches) != 1:
            projected.append({"name": "invalid", "content": action})
            valid.append(0)
        else:
            projected.append({"name": name, "arguments": arguments})
            valid.append(1)
    return projected, valid

def to_numpy(data):
    if isinstance(data, torch.Tensor):
        data = data.detach().cpu().numpy()
    elif isinstance(data, np.ndarray):
        pass
    elif isinstance(data, (int, float, bool, Tuple, List)):
        data = np.array(data)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported type: {type(data)})")
    return data

class EnvironmentManagerBase:
    def __init__(self, envs, projection_f, config):
        """
        Initialize the environment manager.
        
        Parameters:
        - envs: The environment instance, usually a vectorized environment containing multiple sub-environments.
        - projection_f: A function that maps text actions to environment actions.
        - config: Configuration object.
        """
        self.envs = envs
        self.projection_f = projection_f
        self.config = config
        self._seed_use_with_memory = False

    def set_seed_use_with_memory(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
        self._seed_use_with_memory = bool(enabled)

    def reset(self, kwargs) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Reset all environments and return the initial observations.
        Parameters:
        - kwargs (Dict): Additional keyword arguments for resetting the environment.

        Returns:
        - next_observations (Dict):
          - 'text' (None or List[str]): The textual observation.
          - 'image' (np.ndarray or torch.Tensor): The image observation as either a NumPy array or a PyTorch tensor.
          - 'anchor' (None or Any): Anchor observation without any histories or additional info. (for GiGPO only).
        """
        obs, infos = self.envs.reset()
        return {'text': None, 'image': obs, 'anchor': None}, infos
    
    def step(self, text_actions: List[str]):
        """
        Execute text actions and return the next state, rewards, done flags, and additional information.
        
        Parameters:
        - text_actions (List[str]): A list of text actions to execute.
        
        Returns:
        - next_observations (Dict):
          - 'text' (None or List[str]): The textual observation.
          - 'image' (np.ndarray or torch.Tensor): The image observation as either a NumPy array or a PyTorch tensor.
          - 'anchor' (None or Any): Anchor observation without any histories or additional info. (for GiGPO only).
        - rewards (np.ndarry or torch.Tensor): The rewards returned by the environment.
        - dones (np.ndarray or torch.Tensor): Done flags indicating which environments have completed.
        - infos (List[Dict]): Additional environment information.
        
        Exceptions:
        - NotImplementedError: If an observation key is not in ('text', 'image').
        """
        actions, valids = self.projection_f(text_actions)
        next_obs, rewards, dones, infos = self.envs.step(actions)

        next_observations = {
            'text': None, # Implement this if needed
            'image': next_obs,
            'anchor': None # For GiGPO/SEED only. anchor observation without histories, injected skills, etc. Implement this if needed
        }
        # add action_valid to infos
        for i, info in enumerate(infos):
            info['is_action_valid'] = to_numpy(valids[i])

        rewards = to_numpy(rewards)
        dones = to_numpy(dones)
        
        return next_observations, rewards, dones, infos

    def build_text_obs(self,) -> List[str]:
        """
        This function builds the text observation for the agent.
        
        Returns:
        - postprocess_text_obs (List[str]): A list of processed text observations.
        """
        pass

    def close(self) -> None:
        """
        Close the environment and release resources.
        """
        self.envs.close()

    def close_sessions(self) -> None:
        close_sessions = getattr(self.envs, "close_sessions", None)
        if close_sessions is not None:
            close_sessions()

    def success_evaluator(self, *args, **kwargs) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]:
        """
        Evaluate if the episodes are successful or not. 
        (Default) implementation is to check info['won'] of the last step.
        
        Returns:
        - success (np.ndarray or torch.Tensor): 1 if the episode is successful, 0 otherwise.
        """
        total_infos = kwargs['total_infos']
        total_batch_list = kwargs['total_batch_list']
        batch_size = len(total_batch_list)
        
        success = defaultdict(list)
        
        for bs in range(batch_size):
            self._process_batch(bs, total_batch_list, total_infos, success)
        
        assert len(success['success_rate']) == batch_size

        return {key: np.array(value) for key, value in success.items()}
    
    def _process_batch(self, batch_idx, total_batch_list, total_infos, success):
        for i in reversed(range(len(total_batch_list[batch_idx]))):
            batch_item = total_batch_list[batch_idx][i]
            if batch_item['active_masks']:
                info = total_infos[batch_idx][i]
                won_value = float(info['won'])
                success['success_rate'].append(won_value)
                return
            
    def save_image(self, image, step):
        """
        Save an image to a file.
        
        Parameters:
        - image (np.ndarray or torch.Tensor): The image to save.
        - path (str): The path to save the image.
        """
        path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), os.path.join("images", self.config.env.env_name))
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            os.makedirs(path)
        path = os.path.join(path, f"step{step}.png")
        if isinstance(image, torch.Tensor):
            image = image.detach().cpu().numpy()
        if isinstance(image, np.ndarray):
            pass
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported type: {type(image)})")
        
        if len(image.shape) == 4:
            image = image[0]
        if image.shape[0] == 3:
            image = np.transpose(image, (1, 2, 0))
        if image.max() <= 1.0:
            image = (image * 255)

        image = image.astype(np.uint8)
        
        from PIL import Image
        image = Image.fromarray(image)
        image.save(path)

        config = {

    def _request(self, payload: dict) -> dict:

        return response["tasks"], [{"scenario": item["scenario"]} for item in items]

class AWMEnvironmentManager(EnvironmentManagerBase):
    """Prompt/history adapter for AgentWorldModel MCP environments."""

    def __init__(self, envs, projection_f, config):
        self.memory = SimpleMemory()
        self.tasks = []
        super().__init__(envs, projection_f, config)

    def reset(self, kwargs):
        tasks, infos = self.envs.reset(kwargs)
        self.tasks = list(tasks)
        self.memory.reset(batch_size=len(tasks))
        initial = self.build_text_obs(init=True)
        observations = {
            "text": initial,
            "text_base": initial.copy(),
            "image": None,
            "anchor": list(tasks),
        }
        return observations, infos

    def step(self, text_actions: List[str]):
        actions, valids = self.projection_f(text_actions)
        text_obs, rewards, dones, infos = self.envs.step(actions)
        self.memory.store({"action": text_actions, "observation": text_obs})
        next_text = self.build_text_obs()
        for idx, info in enumerate(infos):
            # Preserve semantic MCP errors reported by the bridge while also
            # honoring projection-level format validation.
            info["is_action_valid"] = to_numpy(
                bool(valids[idx]) and bool(info.get("is_action_valid", True))
            )
        return {
            "text": next_text,
            "text_base": next_text.copy(),
            "image": None,
            "anchor": text_obs,
        }, to_numpy(rewards), to_numpy(dones), infos

    def build_text_obs(self, init=False):
        prompts = []
        history_length = int(self.config.env.history_length)
        for idx, task in enumerate(self.tasks):
            if init or not self.memory[idx]:
                prompts.append(AWM_INITIAL_TEMPLATE.format(
                    system_prompt=AWM_SYSTEM_PROMPT, task_description=task,
                ))
                continue
            recent = self.memory[idx][-history_length:] if history_length > 0 else self.memory[idx]
            history = []
            for turn, item in enumerate(recent, 1):
                history.append(f"Assistant {turn}:\n{item['action']}\nTool {turn}:\n{item['observation']}")
            prompts.append(AWM_STEP_TEMPLATE.format(
                system_prompt=AWM_SYSTEM_PROMPT,
                task_description=task,
                history="\n\n".join(history),
            ))
        return prompts

    37	def collate_fn(data_list: list[dict]) -> dict:
    38	    """
    39	    Collate a batch of sample dicts into batched tensors and arrays.
    40	
    41	    Args:
    42	        data_list: List of dicts mapping feature names to torch.Tensor or other values.
    43	
    44	    Returns:
    45	        Dict where tensor entries are stacked into a torch.Tensor of shape
    46	        (batch_size, *dims) and non-tensor entries are converted to
    47	        np.ndarray of dtype object with shape (batch_size,).
    48	    """
    49	    tensors = defaultdict(list)
    50	    non_tensors = defaultdict(list)
    51	
    52	    for data in data_list:
    53	        for key, val in data.items():
    54	            if isinstance(val, torch.Tensor):
    55	                tensors[key].append(val)
    56	            else:
    57	                non_tensors[key].append(val)
    58	
    59	    for key, val in tensors.items():
    60	        tensors[key] = torch.stack(val, dim=0)
    61	
    62	    for key, val in non_tensors.items():
    63	        non_tensors[key] = np.array(val, dtype=object)
    64	
    65	    return {**tensors, **non_tensors}

    def build_text_prompt_batch(

        )

    def preprocess_single_sample(
        self,
        item: int,
        gen_batch: DataProto,
        obs: Dict,
    ):
        """
        Process a single observation sample, organizing environment observations (text and/or images) 
        into a format processable by the model.
        
        Parameters:
            item (int): Sample index in the batch
            gen_batch (DataProto): Batch data containing original prompts
            obs (Dict): Environment observation, may contain 'text', 'image', 'anchor' keys
        
        Returns:
            dict: Contains processed input data such as input_ids, attention_mask, etc.
        """

        raw_prompt = gen_batch.non_tensor_batch['raw_prompt'][item]
        data_source = gen_batch.non_tensor_batch['data_source'][item]
        apply_chat_template_kwargs = self.config.data.get("apply_chat_template_kwargs", {})
        
        # Get observation components
        obs_texts = obs.get('text', None)
        obs_base_texts = obs.get('text_base', None)
        obs_images = obs.get('image', None)
        obs_anchors = obs.get('anchor', None)
        obs_text = obs_texts[item] if obs_texts is not None else None
        obs_text_base = obs_base_texts[item] if obs_base_texts is not None else obs_text
        obs_image = obs_images[item] if obs_images is not None else None
        obs_anchor = obs_anchors[item] if obs_anchors is not None else None
        is_multi_modal = obs_image is not None

        _obs_anchor = torch_to_numpy(obs_anchor, is_object=True) if isinstance(obs_anchor, torch.Tensor) else obs_anchor

        # Build chat structure
        # obs_content = raw_prompt[0]['content']
        # if '<image>' in obs_content: 
        #     obs_content = obs_content.replace('<image>', '')

        # Build chat structure
        obs_content = ''
        if obs_text is not None:
            obs_content += obs_text
        else:
            print(f"Warning: No text observation found!")

        
        chat = np.array([{
            "content": obs_content,
            "role": "user",
        }])
        
        # Apply chat template
        prompt_with_chat_template = self.tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            chat,
            add_generation_prompt=True,
            tokenize=False,
            **apply_chat_template_kwargs
        )
        
        # Initialize return dict
        row_dict = {}
        
        # Process multimodal data
        if is_multi_modal:
            # Replace image placeholder with vision tokens
            raw_prompt = prompt_with_chat_template.replace('<image>', '<|vision_start|><|image_pad|><|vision_end|>')
            row_dict['multi_modal_data'] = {'image': [process_image(self._image_to_uint8_array(obs_image))]}
            image_inputs = self.processor.image_processor(row_dict['multi_modal_data']['image'], return_tensors='pt')
            image_grid_thw = image_inputs['image_grid_thw']
            row_dict['multi_modal_inputs'] = {key: val for key, val in image_inputs.items()}
            if image_grid_thw is not None:
                merge_length = self.processor.image_processor.merge_size**2
                index = 0
                while '<image>' in prompt_with_chat_template:
                    prompt_with_chat_template = prompt_with_chat_template.replace(
                        '<image>',
                        '<|vision_start|>' + '<|placeholder|>' * (image_grid_thw[index].prod() // merge_length) +
                        '<|vision_end|>',
                        1,
                    )
                    index += 1

                prompt_with_chat_template = prompt_with_chat_template.replace('<|placeholder|>',
                                                                                self.processor.image_token)

        else:
            raw_prompt = prompt_with_chat_template
        
        input_ids, attention_mask = verl_F.tokenize_and_postprocess_data(prompt=prompt_with_chat_template,
                                                                            tokenizer=self.tokenizer,
                                                                            max_length=self.config.data.max_prompt_length,
                                                                            pad_token_id=self.tokenizer.pad_token_id,
                                                                            left_pad=True,
                                                                            truncation=self.config.data.truncation,)
        
        

        if is_multi_modal:

            if "Qwen3VLProcessor" in self.processor.__class__.__name__:
                from verl.models.transformers.qwen3_vl import get_rope_index
            else:
                from verl.models.transformers.qwen2_vl import get_rope_index

            vision_position_ids = get_rope_index(
                self.processor,
                input_ids=input_ids[0],
                image_grid_thw=image_grid_thw,
                attention_mask=attention_mask[0],
            )  # (3, seq_length)
            valid_mask = attention_mask[0].bool()
            text_position_ids = torch.ones((1, len(input_ids[0])), dtype=torch.long)
            text_position_ids[0, valid_mask] = torch.arange(valid_mask.sum().item())
            position_ids = [torch.cat((text_position_ids, vision_position_ids), dim=0)]  # (1, 4, seq_length)
        else:
            position_ids = compute_position_id_with_mask(attention_mask)

        raw_prompt_ids = self.tokenizer.encode(raw_prompt, add_special_tokens=False)
        if len(raw_prompt_ids) > self.config.data.max_prompt_length:
            if self.config.data.truncation == "left":
                raw_prompt_ids = raw_prompt_ids[-self.config.data.max_prompt_length :]
            elif self.config.data.truncation == "right":
                raw_prompt_ids = raw_prompt_ids[: self.config.data.max_prompt_length]
            elif self.config.data.truncation == "middle":
                left_half = self.config.data.max_prompt_length // 2
                right_half = self.config.data.max_prompt_length - left_half
                raw_prompt_ids = raw_prompt_ids[:left_half] + raw_prompt_ids[-right_half:]
            elif self.config.data.truncation == "error":
                raise RuntimeError(f"Prompt length {len(raw_prompt_ids)} is longer than {self.config.data.max_prompt_length}.")

        # Build final output dict
        row_dict.update({
            'input_ids': input_ids[0],
            'attention_mask': attention_mask[0],
            'position_ids': position_ids[0],
            'raw_prompt_ids': raw_prompt_ids,
            'anchor_obs': _obs_anchor,
            'obs_text': obs_content,
            'obs_text_base': "" if obs_text_base is None else str(obs_text_base),
            'index': item,
            'data_source': data_source
        })

        if self.config.data.get('return_raw_chat', False):
            row_dict['raw_prompt'] = chat.tolist()
        
        return row_dict

    def preprocess_batch(
        self,
        gen_batch: DataProto, 
        obs: Dict, 
    ) -> DataProto:
        """
        Process a batch of observation samples, converting environment observations into model-processable format.
        
        Parameters:
            gen_batch (DataProto): Batch data containing original prompts
            obs (Dict): Environment observation dictionary
                - 'text' (None or List[str]): Text observation data
                - 'image' (np.ndarray or torch.Tensor): Image observation data
                - 'anchor' (None or Any): Anchor observation without any histories or additional info. (for GiGPO only).
        
        Returns:

        """
        batch_size = len(gen_batch.batch['input_ids'])
        processed_samples = []
            batch_size,
            num_trajectories,
            self.config.algorithm.seed.selector,
            self.config.algorithm.seed.analysis_backend,
            analysis_mode,

        )
        metrics["seed/analysis_mode_teacher_bootstrap"] = 1.0 if not failed_only else 0.0
        metrics["seed/analysis_mode_failed_episode_opd"] = 1.0 if failed_only else 0.0

        if "obs_text" not in batch.non_tensor_batch:
            module_logger.warning("SEED teacher signal skipped because obs_text is missing from the rollout batch.")
            batch.batch["teacher_log_prob"] = zero_teacher_log_prob
            batch.batch["episode_teacher_log_prob"] = zero_teacher_log_prob.clone()
            batch.batch["step_teacher_log_prob"] = zero_teacher_log_prob.clone()
            batch.batch["critical_step_mask"] = zero_critical_mask
            batch.batch["step_skill_mask"] = zero_step_skill_mask
            metrics["seed/critical_step_ratio"] = 0.0
            metrics["seed/teacher_batch_size"] = 0.0
            metrics["seed/teacher_available"] = 0.0
            metrics["seed/episode_skill_teacher/enabled"] = 0.0
            metrics["seed/step_skill_teacher/step_skill_step_ratio"] = 0.0
            metrics["seed/step_skill_teacher/step_skills_applied"] = 0.0
            return batch

        step_indices = core_seed.build_traj_step_indices(batch.non_tensor_batch["traj_uid"])
        batch.non_tensor_batch["step_idx"] = step_indices

        selector = self.config.algorithm.seed.selector
        analyzer = self._lazy_init_seed_analyzer()

def immutable_revision(value):
    if not value or not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{40}", value):

def download_data(repo_id, revision):

                                     allow_patterns=["rl/*", "runtime/*", "manifest.json"]))
    root = ROOT / "data/AgentWorldModel-1K"

               (snapshot / "rl/validation.parquet", root / "verl/test.parquet")]
    names = ["gen_db", "gen_envs", "gen_sample", "gen_tasks", "gen_verifier.pure_code"]
    mapping += [(snapshot / "runtime" / (name + ".jsonl"), root / (name + ".jsonl")) for name in names]
    for source, target in mapping:
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if not target.exists():

    manifest = json.loads((ROOT.parent / "environment/data_manifest.json").read_text())
    expected = {item["path"]: item for item in manifest["files"]}

            digest = hashlib.file_digest(stream, "sha256").hexdigest()
        if target.stat().st_size != item["bytes"] or digest != item["sha256"]:

            assert item["task"] == tasks[scenario][index], (scenario, index)

        splits[split] = rows
    assert not keys["train"] & keys["test"], "train/test overlap"
    assert len(keys["train"] | keys["test"]) == sum(len(t) for t in tasks.values())

def smoke(config, output, splits):
    # Load the packaged environment directly, without importing unrelated envs.
    path = ROOT / "idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/envs.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("packaged_awm_env", path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    selected = []
    seen = set()
    for rows in (splits["train"], splits["test"], splits["train"][1:]):
        for row in rows:
            item = row["env_kwargs"]
            if item["scenario"] not in seen:
                selected.append(item)
                seen.add(item["scenario"])
                break
    env = module.AWMMCPVectorEnv(len(selected), 1, config.env)
    try:
        tasks, _ = env.reset(selected)
        observations, _, dones, infos = env.step([{"name": "list_tools", "arguments": None}] * len(selected))
        for item, observation, done, info in zip(selected, observations, dones, infos):
            if done or info.get("reward_type") == "environment_error":
                raise RuntimeError(f"Environment startup failed: {item['scenario']}: {info}")

        _, rewards, dones, infos = env.step([{"name": "final", "content": "Smoke test, no task actions performed."}] * len(selected))
        assert all(dones), "final action did not terminate"

    args, overrides = parser.parse_known_args()

    if args.download_data:

    if args.smoke:

        command += ["hydra.run.dir=" + str(output)]
        if args.config_only:

        with log_path.open("wb") as log:

        print(f"Exit code: {result.returncode}; combined stdout/stderr: {log_path}")

        }

def batch_test_environments(env_configs: list[dict], max_workers: int = 8) -> list[tuple[bool, str, dict]]:
    if not env_configs:
        return []
    
    logger.info(f"testing {len(env_configs)} environments in parallel (max_workers={max_workers})...")
    
    results: list[tuple[bool, str, dict]] = [None] * len(env_configs)
    passed = 0
    failed = 0
    
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as executor:
        future_to_idx = {   
            executor.submit(test_run_specific_env, idx, config): idx
            for idx, config in enumerate(env_configs)
        }
        
        pbar = tqdm(total=len(env_configs), desc="Testing envs", unit="env")
        pbar.set_postfix(passed=passed, failed=failed)
        
        for future in as_completed(future_to_idx):
            idx = future_to_idx[future]
            try:
                result = future.result()
                results[idx] = result
                scenario_name = env_configs[idx]['scenario']
                if result[0]:
                    passed += 1
                    logger.debug(f"{scenario_name}: test passed")
                else:
                    failed += 1
                    logger.debug(f"{scenario_name}: test failed due to {result}")
            except Exception as e:
                failed += 1
                logger.error(f"test execution failed for index {idx}: {e}")
                results[idx] = (False, str(e), env_configs[idx])
            
            pbar.set_postfix(passed=passed, failed=failed)
            pbar.update(1)
        
        pbar.close()
    
    logger.info(f"batch test done: {passed} passed, {failed} failed out of {len(env_configs)} total")
    return results

def execute_sample_data(db_path: str, sample_data: dict, scenario_name: str) -> tuple[int, int, set[str]]:
    
    db_file = Path(db_path)
    if not db_file.exists():
        logger.error(f"Database not found: {db_path}, skipping data insertion")
        return 0, 0, {"Database file not found"}

    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    
    cursor.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;")
    
    total_statements = 0
    successful_inserts = 0
    failed_inserts = 0
    error_messages: set[str] = set()
    
    try:
        for table_data in sample_data.get("tables", []):
            table_name = table_data.get("table_name", "unknown")
            insert_statements = table_data.get("insert_statements", [])
            
            
            for stmt in insert_statements:
                total_statements += 1
                try:
                    cursor.execute(stmt)
                    successful_inserts += 1
                except sqlite3.IntegrityError as e:
                    failed_inserts += 1
                    error_messages.add(f"Table {table_name} - IntegrityError: {str(e)[:1000]}")
                except sqlite3.Error as e:
                    failed_inserts += 1
                    error_messages.add(f"Table {table_name} - SQLError: {str(e)[:1000]}\nStatement: {stmt[:1000]}")
        
        conn.commit()
        logger.info(f"{scenario_name}: {successful_inserts}/{total_statements} statements executed with {failed_inserts} failures")
        
    except Exception as e:
        conn.rollback()
        error_messages.add(f"Transaction failed: {str(e)}")
        raise e
    finally:
        conn.close()
    
    return successful_inserts, failed_inserts, error_messages

"""JSON-lines bridge to Agent World Model's Python 3.12 MCP runtime."""

import json
import os
import shutil

# Reward contract used by the AWM RL environment.  Unknown verifier/judge
# outcomes intentionally receive zero rather than being treated as failures.
REWARD_BY_TYPE = {
    "complete": 1.0,
    "completed": 1.0,
    "incomplete": 0.1,
    "partially_completed": 0.1,
    "partial": 0.1,
    # Pure-code verifiers use `others` for an unsuccessful completion check;
    # unsuccessful/unknown outcomes are agent/environment errors and receive
    # zero task reward.
    "others": 0.0,
    "agent_error": 0.0,
    "environment_error": 0.0,
    "server_error": 0.0,
    "judge_error": 0.0,
    "format_error": -1.0,
    "tool_not_found": -1.0,
    "invalid_args": -1.0,
}

# Judge labels that count as a successful / partial task outcome.  Terminal
# shaping below only rewrites these; environment/agent errors stay as-is.
_COMPLETE_TYPES = {"complete", "completed"}
_INCOMPLETE_TYPES = {"incomplete", "partially_completed", "partial"}
# Identical successful tool calls (same name + arguments) this many times in a
# row end the episode and run the verifier instead of letting the agent loop.
DEFAULT_REPEAT_SUCCESS_TERMINATE_K = 5


@dataclass
class Session:
    scenario: str
    task_idx: int
    task: str
    output_dir: str
    db_path: str
    server: object | None
    mcp: MCPToolExecutor | None
    tools_text: str
    verifier: dict
    steps: int = 0
    done: bool = False
    trajectory: list[dict] | None = None
    startup_error: str | None = None
    # Consecutive MCP service failures are tracked separately from malformed
    # model actions.  A repeated identical failure indicates an environment
    # problem rather than an agent error.
    last_mcp_error: str | None = None
    mcp_error_streak: int = 0
    last_success_call_key: str | None = None
    success_call_streak: int = 0


class Bridge:
    def __init__(self, config: dict):
        self.root = Path(config["awm_root"])
        self.data = Path(config["data_root"])
        self.max_steps = int(config["max_steps"])
        self.tool_timeout = float(config.get("tool_timeout", 60))
        self.reward_mode = str(config.get("reward_mode", "code")).lower()
        if self.reward_mode not in {"code", "sql"}:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported reward_mode: {self.reward_mode}; expected code or sql")

        self.judge_api_key = str(config.get("judge_api_key", "EMPTY"))
        self.judge_model = str(config.get("judge_model", ""))
        self.judge_timeout = float(config.get("judge_timeout", 120))
        self.judge_max_retries = int(config.get("judge_max_retries", 3))
        self.judge_concurrency = min(10, max(1, int(config.get("judge_concurrency", 10))))
        self.judge_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(self.judge_concurrency)
        # Starting hundreds of MCP subprocesses at once can starve the
        # readiness probes and make otherwise healthy servers miss the window.
        self.startup_concurrency = max(1, int(config.get("startup_concurrency", 32)))
        self.startup_semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(self.startup_concurrency)
        self.repeat_success_terminate_k = max(
            2, int(config.get("repeat_success_terminate_k", DEFAULT_REPEAT_SUCCESS_TERMINATE_K))
        )
        work_root = config.get("work_root")

        # rollout tensors.  The trainer only propagates a subset of env info,

        self.judge_log_path = self.work_root / "llm_judge.jsonl"
        # The verifier reads these in the isolated AWM subprocess.
        os.environ["AWM_JUDGE_TIMEOUT"] = str(self.judge_timeout)
        os.environ["AWM_JUDGE_MAX_RETRIES"] = str(self.judge_max_retries)
        self.sessions: list[Session] = []
        verifier_file = "gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl" if self.reward_mode == "code" else "gen_verifier.jsonl"

    def _record_judge(
        self,
        session: Session,
        reward_type: str,
        verifier_result: dict,
        judge_result: dict | None,
        shaped_reward_type: str | None = None,
        ended_with_final: bool | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Append one complete Judge decision to the bridge-owned JSONL log."""
        entry = {
            "timestamp": time.time(),
            "scenario": session.scenario,
            "task_idx": session.task_idx,
            "task": session.task,
            "steps": len(session.trajectory or []),
            "reward_type": reward_type,
            "verifier_result": verifier_result,
            "llm_judge": judge_result,
        }
        if shaped_reward_type is not None:
            entry["shaped_reward_type"] = shaped_reward_type
        if ended_with_final is not None:
            entry["ended_with_final"] = ended_with_final
        with self.judge_log_path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(entry, ensure_ascii=False, default=str) + "\n")

    async def _stop_server(self, proc):
        if proc is None:
            return
        try:
            pgid = os.getpgid(proc.pid)
        except ProcessLookupError:
            pgid = None
        if pgid is not None:
            try:
                os.killpg(pgid, signal.SIGTERM)
                await asyncio.to_thread(proc.wait, 5)
            except Exception:
                pass
            # awm.core.server launches uvicorn through a shell; clean any group remnants.
            try:
                os.killpg(pgid, signal.SIGKILL)
            except ProcessLookupError:
                pass
        for pipe in (proc.stdout, proc.stderr):
            if pipe:
                pipe.close()

    async def close(self):
        await self.close_sessions()

    async def close_sessions(self):
        for session in self.sessions:
            proc = session.server
            await self._stop_server(proc)
        self.sessions = []

            *(start_limited(i, item) for i, item in enumerate(items)),
            return_exceptions=True,

        errors = [result for result in results if isinstance(result, BaseException)]

            # Unexpected bridge-level errors are still fatal; individual task
            # startup failures are represented by placeholder sessions above.
            await self.close()
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to start {len(errors)} AWM environment(s): {errors[0]}")

    async def _verify(self, session: Session, final_answer: str) -> tuple[float, dict, dict, dict | None, str]:

    @staticmethod
    def _normalize_reward_type(reward_type: str | None) -> str:
        return str(reward_type or "").strip().lower().replace("-", "_").replace(" ", "_")

    def _success_call_key(name: str, tool_name: str | None, tool_args) -> str | None:
        """Stable identity for a successful list_tools / call_tool action."""
        if name == "list_tools":
            return "list_tools"
        if name != "call_tool" or not tool_name:

        try:
            args_repr = json.dumps(tool_args, sort_keys=True, default=str, ensure_ascii=False)
        except TypeError:

        return f"call_tool:{tool_name}:{args_repr}"

    def _shape_terminal_reward(self, name: str, reward: float, verify_info: dict) -> tuple[float, dict]:
        """Rewrite complete/incomplete when the episode did not end on a final answer.

        incomplete + no final answer -> -1.0
